headline: Evidence-gated authority in language-model review trades fewer corruptions of correct proposals for missed welfare-only repairs
summary: In a September 2026 paper, Fuad Ali compares broad reviewer override with a rule that lets a reviewer replace an upstream proposal only after it supplies a mechanically valid certificate of a binding-constraint violation and a compliant repair. The paper reports paired experiments with Qwen3-8B and Mistral-Small-24B on 96 synthetic spatial-policy tasks and a 96-task portfolio-transfer benchmark. The gate prevents changes to correct proposals by construction, but also bars welfare improvements to compliant, suboptimal proposals. A prospective retain/replace/escalate interface protects correct proposals for Qwen, which then declines welfare-only repairs; Mistral still replaces and corrupts all 48 correct proposals in that test. These are author-reported results from quantized local models and structured synthetic tasks, not evidence of deployment prevalence or a model-independent safety guarantee.
